Simple Rules For a Simple Type System (mi'e la Ctefà'o)

Keep in mind that all of this is very important to fixing how the pro-bridi "instantiate", which is crucial for '''xoi''' and '''soi''' to work properly (and thereby, the case tags ('''sumtcita''')).

# '''All bridi always have a type.''' A bridi type is permanent and never changes or disappears, neither through pro-bridi instantation or macro<ref>I think of any Lojban construct (lo-ku, noi-ku'o, na-ku) as a macro.</ref> expansion. When you create a bridi, you create its type as well.
# '''There exists a default bridi type even when one is not explicitly specified''' (just like NA-s "ja'a" always exist before any bridi with no explicit NA). '''This type is "su'u".''' '''.i broda''' and '''.i su'u broda ''[kei]''''' are equivalent<ref>And putting something in a "su'u" or a NU does not affect assertion in any way. Assertion is NA ("ja'a" for assertion, "'''na'''" for negation), not NU. Not even da'i affects assertion, you simply assert or negate something in an imaginary context. And again you claim something by asserting it with that "default ja'a" (or claim something is false with an explicit "'''na'''".</ref>.
#* Equivalent except that if we put the "kei" in there we can refer to everything inside the expression (which is what xoi and soi does!) through its "x1".
#** And yes, if we do that we sort of (see below) make a selbri out of the expression, becoming '''lo su'u broda''' if we "sumtify" it, that we can use to include everything inside it. Which is what '''xoi''' and '''soi''' does!.
#*** And yes you can do '''.i su'u su'u broda ''[kei] [kei]''''', or put a hundred su'u after each other, but you don't have to do that! NU is not something you can expand! It is an encapsulation, not an expandable construct. Only use as many "su'u"/NU as you need!
#** Consider su'u more as "expression" than "abstraction". Main difference between "su'u" and "du'u" is that "du'u" excludes any other NU while "su'u" does not. See below.
# '''Bridi type is sticky and "inherits" through pro-bridi.''' Any relevant NU are considered to be contained in the pro-bridi "instantation" ('''lo no'a''' is all we need, as the type will follow with the no'a).
#* This is *important* because the adverbial clauses need to get the right NU/bridi-type from the "lo no'a" to refer to the same bridi!
----------
<references />


As for the main difference among the NU:
* "su'u" is all-inclusive and may be any of the other NU.
* "non-su'u" (like "du'u") are all-exclusive and exclude any other NU than themselves.


The NU-x2 places are not (yet) covered by this idea.

Keep in mind that the "x1" of any NU refers to the whole expression, not any single place inside it.

As for how to integrate this properly into existing usage, work is currently under way.



'''The bridi, the cu, the NA and the NU'''

{.i broda}

{.i [cu] broda [vau]} (Note: That "cu" only works with the new connective system.)

{.i [cu] [NA] broda [vau]} (And NA defaults to "ja'a (ku)")

{.i [NU] [cu] [NA] broda [vau] [kei]
